newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen weak, tone cautious on rupiah.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen weak, tone cautious on rupiah.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen weak on Monday, with market sentiment remaining cautious as regional currency volatility spilled over to the rupiah, brokers said.
"Overall sentiment is likely to remain cautious after volatility in some regional currencies spilled over onto the rupiah," one broker with a foreign brokerage firm said.
The Indonesian rupiah fell to 2,464/68 against the dollar at 0130 GMT on Monday against an opening of 2,451/55.

The central bank widened its intervention band to 12 percent from eight percent last Friday in a move operators said was designed to pre-empt possible turbulence of the rupiah after speculators launched an attack on the regional currencies.
Brokers said the cautious sentiment was likely to prompt further profit-taking, particularly in liquid blue-chips.
The Jakarta composite index fell 5.74 points to close at 723.42 points on Friday. The index was off 13.18 points, or 1.80 percent, last week. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364

Brokers said reports on Monday that Moody's Investor Service has revised its ratings outlook for Indonesian state banks to uncertain from stable pending a decision on planned mergers among the seven institutions, were likely to further weaken sentiment in the sector.
Bank BNI is the only state-owned listed bank. BNI fell 25 rupiah to 1,500 rupiah, with some 1.8 million shares traded.
Second-liner Alumindo was among the most active stocks, as it rose 100 rupiah to 1,325 rupiah, on reports the firm would secure a large amount of loans for expansion, brokers said.
